# Tactile model description: wp

## Overview

This overview is plain English. The detailed sections after it give exact positions and each starts with a heading, so you can skip to the one you want.

This model covers about 3.0 km east-west by 3.0 km north-south. North is the far edge. Heights are exaggerated 1.5 times.

Ground elevation runs from about 2720 m in the north-west up to about 3260 m in the south-west, a
difference of about 550 m. The highest ground is in the west, north-east and south-west. The lowest
ground is in the north-west, middle and north.

The longest features:

- Fraser River is a river about 4.2 km long. It generally flows north-west, and wanders east and
  west along the way. It loses about 110 m of elevation along the way, and the water then leaves the
  map at the north edge.
- Main Street is a road about 4.0 km long. It runs nearly straight north-west. Going north-west it
  descends about 110 m, and then leaves the map at the north edge.
- The Gondola is a lift about 1.6 km long. It runs south-west. It climbs about 490 m from the bottom
  terminal in the middle of the map to the top terminal in the south-west part of the map.
- Explorer Express is a lift about 1.4 km long. It runs south. It climbs about 380 m from the bottom
  terminal in the west part of the map to the top terminal in the south-west part of the map.
- Jim Creek is a river about 1.1 km long. It generally flows west, and wanders north and south along
  the way. It loses about 40 m of elevation along the way, and the water then meets Fraser River.
- Winter Park Drive is a road about 790 m long. It runs nearly straight north-west. Going north-west
  it descends about 20 m, and then leaves the map at the north edge.

In all, the map has two rivers, three roads and fifteen lifts.

## Summary

- Model: wp
- Footprint: 201.0 mm east-west by 201.2 mm north-south, 58.7 mm tall in total.
- Scale: 1 mm = 15 m horizontally. Vertical exaggeration: 1.5 times.
- Mode: terrain. Tactile profile: standard. Printer: louisville-library.
- Folder: <MODELS>/wp
- STL file: <MODELS>/wp/wp.stl
- Spec file: <MODELS>/wp/spec.json
- Attribution file: <MODELS>/wp/ATTRIBUTION.txt

## Orientation

- North is the far edge, where y is largest. East is the right edge, where x is largest.
- The origin, x = 0 mm and y = 0 mm, is the south-west corner nearest you.

## Line features

### Fraser River (river, style rounded_major), 279 mm long

Fraser River is a river about 4.2 km long. It generally flows north-west, and wanders east and west
along the way. It loses about 110 m of elevation along the way, and the water then leaves the map at
the north edge.

Turn by turn:

- Walked downstream (with the flow): enters the south edge at x = 170 mm, then runs north for 20 mm,
  then north-west for 39 mm, then west for 18 mm, then north-west for 26 mm, then north for 39 mm,
  then north-west for 92 mm, then west for 16 mm, then north-west for 30 mm, then exits the north
  edge at x = 22 mm.

### Main Street (road, style flat_top), 270 mm long

Main Street is a road about 4.0 km long. It runs nearly straight north-west. Going north-west it
descends about 110 m, and then leaves the map at the north edge.

Turn by turn:

- Enters the south edge at x = 165 mm, then runs north for 53 mm, then north-west for 57 mm, then
  north for 44 mm, then north-west for 70 mm, then west for 47 mm, then exits the north edge at
  x = 17 mm.

### The Gondola (lift, style pointed), 109 mm long

The Gondola is a lift about 1.6 km long. It runs south-west. It climbs about 490 m from the bottom
terminal in the middle of the map to the top terminal in the south-west part of the map.

Turn by turn:

- Bottom terminal at x = 97 mm, y = 96 mm, elevation 2771 m. Top terminal at x = 27 mm, y = 13 mm,
  elevation 3259 m. Length 109 mm (1633 m on the ground), heading south-west.

## Crossings and junctions

- Fraser River crosses Main Street at x = 158 mm, y = 30 mm. Main Street is on top (1.5 mm tall
  against 1 mm).
- Fraser River meets Jim Creek at x = 138 mm, y = 50 mm. Fraser River is on top (1 mm tall against
  1 mm).
- Jim Creek crosses Main Street at x = 143 mm, y = 62 mm. Main Street is on top (1.5 mm tall against
  1 mm).
- Fraser River crosses Village Cabriolet at x = 107 mm, y = 78 mm. Village Cabriolet is on top
  (1.2 mm tall against 1 mm).
- Unnamed road crosses Main Street at x = 108 mm, y = 139 mm. Unnamed road is on top (1.5 mm tall
  against 1.5 mm).
- Fraser River crosses Main Street at x = 30 mm, y = 195 mm. Main Street is on top (1.5 mm tall
  against 1 mm).

## Tactile legend

- River: rounded ridge, 1.6 mm wide and 1 mm tall (style rounded_major, from nhd).
- Road: flat-topped ridge, 2 mm wide and 1.5 mm tall (style flat_top, from osm).
- Lift: pointed ridge, 1.2 mm wide and 1.2 mm tall (style pointed, from osm).

## Distortion

- No horizontal distortion: 1 mm = 15 m in every direction.
- Vertical exaggeration is 1.5 times everywhere, so 1 mm of height stands for 10.0 m of real elevation.
